statement: Record 0092 and its evidence are hash bound and are not edited. Six statements in it were false when it was written; each is named here with what is true instead and with what makes the difference measurable now.

supersedes.row: publish-load reports a complete run only when every published identity arrived exactly once.
supersedes.wasWrong: The row was closed on the ledger's separation of AllExpectedSeen from IsExact. The snapshot itself was not linearizable: Read scans the identities one after another while handlers keep counting, so a schedule in which the scan reads an identity, a consumer then makes it a duplicate, and the scan walks on returns the old total and no duplicate at all. A run that had already duplicated a message read as exact.
supersedes.nowTrue: The scenario establishes the order the claim needs and reports it: the three second observation window, then a bounded stop of the bus which returns only once the consumer reports zero activity, then the snapshot. A stop that ran out of its budget is reported as 'inconclusive' rather than exact.

supersedes.row: Two invocations of the same category share no file.
supersedes.wasWrong: The category runner forwarded an arbitrary argument tail to dotnet test. A second --logger, a --results-directory, a --diag, a collector and an MSBuild output override each write outside the root the run owns, and only the options that select tests were refused. The diagnostics README also named a fixed shared path, artifacts/run-output/publish-load.json, for two runs to write in turn.
supersedes.nowTrue: The runner takes no further argument and forwards none; its command line is closed in both directions. The README names no shared path and points at the run root the runner publishes.

supersedes.row: The recovery proof cannot report green for a weaker property.
supersedes.wasWrong: run_broker_category.main held the primary outcome and the cleanup findings in one variable, so a failed unconditional restore and a control thread that was still alive each printed FAIL and returned 0. The observer and controller decisions were also only covered by the two passing broker cases, which exercise the happy path alone.
supersedes.nowTrue: execute() produces the outcome, teardown() returns findings and never raises, and a cleanup finding makes an otherwise green run red while a primary failure keeps its own exit code. Eight isolated cases drive main() and the control thread; fifteen cases drive the outage boundary and the endpoint observer directly.
supersedes.provenBy: record-0094/counterexample-replay.json, rows teardown-false-green-restore, teardown-false-green-controller, teardown-false-green-down, controller-thread-exception, controller-stop-during-readiness and outage-broker-not-started

supersedes.row: A capability verified through another one is really exercised by that one's run.
supersedes.wasWrong: resolve_indirect_verification searched raw source text, so a file containing only 'namespace Proof.Anchor; public class WordsOnly { }' satisfied an anchor, and the StateMachineVisualizer anchor was the whole namespace ViciOne.ServiceBus.Tests.SagaStateMachineTests.Automatonymous, which holds many unrelated tests.
supersedes.nowTrue: An anchor is a category and an exact fixture. Before a run it has to be a class of that category's test project, declared in a file that carries a test attribute, with comments removed and a namespace refused. During the run the category runner requires at least one executed TRX identity whose fixture equals the anchor, and records which identities carried it.
supersedes.provenBy: record-0094/anchor-binding.json and record-0094/counterexample-replay.json, rows anchor-namespace, anchor-comment, anchor-ordinary-class and anchor-not-executed

supersedes.row: No project can leave the central build contract.
supersedes.wasWrong: The rule searched exact XML text. Three executed counterexamples were accepted: RestoreLockedMode written as False beside a project-written RestoreLockedModeFromCommandLine, a conditional ImportDirectoryBuildTargets, and a conditional DirectoryBuildTargetsPath redirect. Only .csproj files were read at all.
supersedes.nowTrue: The MSBuild XML is parsed. Six properties are reserved for the two root files and refused in any project, any project-local props or targets, and any Directory.Build.props below the root, regardless of condition, case, whitespace or value; every PropertyGroup is read wherever it stands.
supersedes.provenBy: record-0094/counterexample-replay.json, rows central-locked-mode-case, central-conditional-import and central-conditional-redirect

supersedes.row: Every required category runs through the count gate and records its floor.
supersedes.wasWrong: Two statements underneath it were false. The required RabbitMQ step was missing the backslash after its --evidence-dir line, so the shell built two commands and the job could not run. And check_executed_floor read a top level 'categories' object which the verification model has not had since it replaced the two files before it, so its loop ran over nothing and the rule passed for every repository.
supersedes.nowTrue: The step is repaired, and the validator reconstructs the effective command of every run step and parses each runner call against that runner's own command line. The floor rule reads the declared runs of the model.

supersedes.row: The diagnostics correctness cases gate the tool.
supersedes.wasWrong: Stated in the diagnostics README and in the rationale of the model, while no required job started them. The benchmarks job built the engineering solution and ran the benchmark harness project alone.
supersedes.nowTrue: They run as the required category 'diagnostics' of that same job, through tools/ci/run_test_category.py, with a measured floor of 35 executed cases and a run-owned result upload.
